title: privnet security-controls Terraform package: security-groups, nacls, private-dns, and egress governance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform package that codifies Redwood's recommended VPC security posture for private (VPC) deployments. The module must provide composable building blocks for: 1) security groups with environment-aware default rules and explicit allow-lists; 2) stateless NACL templates for subnet-level hardening; 3) private Route53 zone creation and conditional forwarding to on-prem DNS for hybrid customers; and 4) centralized egress governance (CIDR/host allow-lists, explicit deny paths, optional proxy integration). This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and rollout plan for the initial module release. The output should be safe-by-default, configurable, and integrate with existing privnet orchestration templates.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes clear inputs/outputs and examples for three deployment profiles: dev (open egress for diagnostics), staging (restricted egress), and prod (strict allow-list and proxy-only).
Security groups created by the module are taggable and include an allow-list shim for managed services (e.g., metrics, logging, KMS).
NACL baseline denies all inbound by default and documents expected ephemeral exceptions for batch workloads; automated tests validate NACL rule ordering and idempotency.
Private DNS zone provisioning and a conditional forwarding record are created when customer sets onprem_dns=true; integration test demonstrates resolution to a stubbed on-prem resolver.
Egress policy supports both CIDR-based and FQDN-based allow-lists, and can toggle to an egress-proxy endpoint; Terraform plan shows no drift for existing customers when toggling proxy mode.
Module includes automated terratest/unit tests (CI) and a staged rollout plan (canary -> region-wide) with rollback steps documented.
Security team has signed off on the default rule-set and an associated README describes operational runbooks for incidents caused by egress policies.
implementation_notes: Design trade-off: favor explicit allow-lists over host-level deny to simplify audits and reduce accidental blanket-deny during rollouts.
Use separate submodules: sg_core, nacl_core, dns_private, egress_controller to keep interfaces small and testable.
Expose a 'compatibility_mode' flag to map module outputs to existing privnet templates used by early customers (avoids requiring immediate refactors).
Prefer Route53 private hosted zones and conditional forwarders for AWS-first customers; document an on-prem alternative using bind-config templates for air-gapped ops.
Avoid embedding customer secrets in outputs; supply KMS key ARNs as inputs and validate via regex in plan-time checks.
Plan for future integration with Redwood's console: expose telemetry hooks (CloudWatch metrics / Prometheus labels) for SG hit counts and egress denials.
tests: Unit: terraform validate + tflint + custom rule checks (tagging, naming conventions)
Integration: terratest suite that deploys module into a temporary account and validates DNS resolution, SG reachability, and egress proxying
CI Gate: plan must not remove default infra resources; changes to egress allow-lists require 'egress-audit' tag to be present.
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff with Architecture; agreed on submodule decomposition and 'compatibility_mode' requirement.
2026-03-02: Prototype sg_core and nacl_core submodules; initial tflint rules added. QA to pair on NACL edge-case ordering.
2026-03-06: Added private DNS forwarding option; discovered Route53 conditional forwarder cannot be created with cross-account resolver endpoints in our test account — pending ops ticket.
2026-03-10: First PR opened for sg_core (PR #412). Security review requested; adding egress-proxy abstraction in parallel branch.
review_feedback: Security (Jules Kramer): Requested explicit deny rules for uncommon management ports and recommended documenting the incident rollback steps when proxy mode breaks.
Product (Maya Chen): Ask to make env profiles explicit (dev/staging/prod) rather than inferred from tags for clarity in self-serve templates.
SRE (Leo Henriksen): Suggested adding an EndpointHealth resource and a small lambda to report DNS and egress check status to central monitoring; flagged as optional for MVP.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Rolling a strict egress allow-list can break customer workloads. Mitigation: default to permissive for existing infra and provide a 'strict_mode=false' flag; enforce canary rollout with metrics.
Risk: NACL rule ordering causing unexpected traffic drops. Mitigation: include unit tests that validate rule ordering and add documentation with examples for common patterns.
Risk: Cross-account DNS forwarding complexity. Mitigation: provide a clear fallback path (manual on-prem stub) and ops-runbook to complete resolver setup.
next_steps: Address the Route53 cross-account resolver limitation with CloudOps by 2026-03-14 (Ops ticket O-2298).
Complete egress_controller prototype and wire it into PR #428 for combined review.
Add terratest scenario that simulates 'proxy failure' and validates automatic fallback (per rollout policy).
Schedule security review follow-up once sg_core + egress_controller merged into main.
